note.explanation: SI units give people around the world a common way to measure. Base units are the starting units; derived units are made from them. Prefixes show powers of ten, making very large or very small measurements easier to write.
examples: Area = length × breadth = metre × metre = square metre = m².
note.checkAnswer: The unit of area is the square metre, m².
note.simple: Think of base units as the basic building blocks. Derived units combine those blocks, and prefixes tell you how many powers of ten a unit represents.
note.checkQuestion: What is the SI unit and symbol for mass?
note.title: SI units and prefixes
steps: Name the physical quantity and identify its unit.
For a derived unit, write how the quantity is made from other quantities.
Replace each quantity with its SI base unit.
For a prefix, replace it with its power of ten and convert.
note.answer: The SI unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).

mcqs.stem: Which of these is an SI base unit?
rationales: Metre is the SI base unit for length, but it is not the unit asked for here.
Kilogram is one of the seven SI base units.
Newton is a derived SI unit for force.
Second is an SI base unit for time, but not the correct option here.

mcqs.stem: Which SI unit is used for temperature?
rationales: Cubic metre is a derived unit of volume.
Pascal is a derived unit of pressure.
Kelvin is the SI base unit for temperature.
Coulomb is a derived unit of electric charge.

mcqs.stem: Which symbol represents the SI unit of speed?
rationales: m² is the symbol for square metre, the unit of area.
m s⁻¹ means metre per second, the SI unit of speed.
kg is the SI base unit of mass.
m³ is the symbol for cubic metre, the unit of volume.

mcqs.stem: Which symbol represents the SI base unit of electric current?
rationales: A is the symbol for ampere, the SI base unit of electric current.
cd is the symbol for candela, the unit of intensity of light.
mol is the symbol for mole, the unit of amount of substance.
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature.

mcqs.stem: The prefix milli represents which power of ten?
rationales: Milli represents one thousandth, or 10⁻³.
Micro represents 10⁻⁶, not milli.
Kilo represents 10³.
Mega represents 10⁶.
3 km is ten times the given distance.
300 m has not been converted to kilometres.
30 km is one hundred times the given distance.

mcqs.stem: Which of these is the SI unit of area?
rationales: m s⁻¹ is the SI unit of speed.
m² is the SI unit of area.
N is the symbol for newton, the unit of force.
kg is the SI base unit of mass.

mcqs.stem: What is 2000 μs expressed in seconds?
rationales: This is too small by a factor of 1000.
This is too large by a factor of 10⁶.
This is too small by a factor of 10⁶.

written.finalAnswer: Base quantities are independent quantities; derived quantities are obtained from base quantities. SI base units: metre (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), kelvin (K), ampere (A), candela (cd), mole (mol).

examTips: Short-answer questions may ask you to list the seven SI base units, explain why prefixes are used, or interpret a prefixed measurement.
Numerical questions commonly ask you to convert between units or express an answer using a suitable SI prefix or scientific notation.
For method marks, show the conversion factor and intermediate step, then write the final value with its unit.
Be careful with powers of ten: kilo is 10³, milli is 10⁻³, micro is 10⁻⁶ and nano is 10⁻⁹.

explain.title: SI helps everyone measure in a common way
explain.body: SI is the international system of units. Using it helps scientists share and compare observations and results easily.

explain.title: The seven base units
explain.body: The seven base units are metre (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), kelvin (K), ampere (A), candela (cd) and mole (mol). Their values are fixed with reference to international standards.

explain.title: Derived units come from base units
explain.body: The units which can be expressed in terms of base units are called derived units. For example, area is measured in square metres (m²), and speed in metres per second (m s⁻¹).

explain.title: Prefixes show powers of ten
explain.body: Prefixes are the words or symbols added before SI units, such as milli, centi and kilo. They make very large or small quantities more convenient to write.

explain.title: Convert carefully
explain.body: Use the prefix value to convert a measurement. For example, 3000 g = 3000/1000 kg = 3 kg. Keep the unit in your answer.

mistakes: Mixing up unit symbols, such as writing K for kilo instead of kelvin; symbols are case-sensitive.
Forgetting that prefixes represent powers of ten, or using the wrong exponent when converting.
Changing the number but leaving out the unit in the final answer.
Confusing base units with derived units: kilogram is a base unit, while newton and pascal are derived units.
Writing a prefix symbol with the wrong case, such as M for milli instead of m.
